body:
Deriving cryptographic keys from passwords (or other information of lower cryptographic strength) is common in modern applications that handle sensitive data that must be encrypted at rest.

This includes most hard disk encryption, password managers, cryptographic wallets, etc.
By law sensitive data includes personal identifying information. So this control is relevant for most applications. So I suggest to make this a level 2 control.

Add a new control to [11.4](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x20-V11-Cryptography.md#v114-hashing-and-hash-based-functions):
Verify that cryptographic keys are derived from passwords or other information of lower cryptographic strength using a key derivation function with parameter settings configured based on current guidance for key stretching. The settings should balance security and performance to make a brute-force attack against the password (or other information) as challenging as attacking the resulting cryptographic key directly. The cryptographic strength of the derived key should be at least 128 bits of entropy.

comments.body:
If we want this, I would say instead:

> Verify that when the application derives cryptographic keys derived from passwords or other information of lower cryptographic strength, it uses a key derivation function with parameter settings configured based on current guidance for key stretching. The settings should balance security and performance to make a brute-force attack against the password (or other information) as challenging as attacking the resulting cryptographic key directly.

Should we include a section about password based key derivation in the appendix?

Should we say here "approved" password-based key derivation functions? Something like:

> Verify that when the application derives cryptographic keys derived from passwords or other information of lower cryptographic strength, it uses an approved password-based key derivation function with parameter settings configured based on current guidance for key stretching. The settings should balance security and performance to make a brute-force attack against the password (or other information) as challenging as attacking the resulting cryptographic key directly.

About:

> The cryptographic strength of the derived key should be at least 128 bits of entropy.

This part is actually supposed to be covered by the requirements about the key usage anyway so I would drop it here.

I do think we want this in, it's a common use case. I like @randomstuff edits. In particular:

_11.4.4 Verify that when the application derives cryptographic keys derived from passwords or other information of lower cryptographic strength, it uses an approved password-based key derivation function with parameter settings configured based on current guidance for key stretching. The settings should balance security and performance to make a brute-force attack against the password (or other information) as challenging as attacking the resulting cryptographic key directly._

But the proposed requirement still provide some value on top of 11.4.1.

Thanks @randomstuff I believe this is a clash and that the proposed new requirement should actually be merged into this one.

I have been trying to merge these, but I would dare say the are separate issues and I agree with the OP that this should be a separate requirement. @randomstuff do you have suggestions as to how we could merge these? I'm at a loss without it getting very messy.

After some thought, I think it would make more sense to have a separate requirement:

* 11.4.1 is about cryptographic hash functions;
* proposed requirement is about password-based key derivation.

While the latter uses the former, I'd rather not conflate the two in a single requirement: this would cause confusion and a messy/lengthy requirement.
